actor: rival platform or productivity vendor's first-party agent product lead
job: Deciding to embed a maintained open agent harness as the runtime rather than rebuild a proprietary loop, then shipping a branded first-party agent.
outcome: A launch, preview, or technical disclosure naming a tracked open harness as the engine inside the vendor's branded enterprise agent.
motivation: Reimplementing a proprietary runtime offers little edge; embedding the solved open loop lets the vendor compete on controls and distribution.

task.who: Agent-platform product and roadmap function at a second major vendor
task.what: Adopt open harness as runtime, ship branded agent
task.where: The vendor's flagship productivity or platform agent surface
task.when: Across the build-vs-buy and ship runway through 2026
task.why: Open loop is solved; differentiation lives in wrapper and distribution
task.how: Embedding OpenClaw or a peer tracked open harness

actor: enterprise vendor's identity, policy, and data-governance engineering team
job: Building the governed identity, scoped credentials, audit, policy-conformance, and data-protection wrapper that lets an open harness run as a sanctioned enterprise agent.
outcome: A governance layer mature enough that the branded agent ships on the open harness under the vendor's own identity, policy, and data controls.
motivation: The differentiated, hard work for an enterprise vendor is now the governance wrapper, not the commoditized agent loop.

task.who: Identity, compliance, and data-protection engineering inside the vendor
task.what: Wrap open harness in identity, policy, audit controls
task.where: The vendor's enterprise identity and data-governance stack
task.when: During the wrapper build-out runway ahead of launch
task.why: Governance wrapper is the vendor's real source of differentiation
task.how: Scoped identity, audit trails, policy and data-protection enforcement

actor: open agent-harness project maintainer and steward
job: Keeping a tracked open local-agent harness battle-tested, maintained, and cleanly embeddable so an enterprise vendor can adopt it as a runtime rather than rebuild.
outcome: An open harness stable and embeddable enough to be disclosed as the runtime engine inside a second vendor's branded enterprise agent.
motivation: Broad first-party embedding entrenches the harness as the default open agent loop and grows its maintainer ecosystem and relevance.

task.who: Core maintainer and release-engineering community of the open harness
task.what: Maintain and harden the embeddable open agent loop
task.where: The open-source harness project repository and release pipeline
task.when: Continuously through the pre-Q4-2026 adoption runway
task.why: An adoptable, solved loop lets vendors embed rather than rebuild
task.how: Open-source maintenance, hardening, and stable embedding interfaces
